title: far right afd posts historic german state election win exit polls show 2026 09 06
text:
BERLIN, Sept 6 (Reuters) - The far-right Alternative for Germany ​scored a historic victory ‌in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, exit polls ​showed on Sunday, ​dealing a blow to Chancellor ⁠Friedrich Merz's conservatives, ​but it was unclear ​whether the result would be enough to govern.
The AfD won ​44.5% of the vote, ​according to exit polls of ‌ARD ⁠broadcaster, up from 20.8% in 2021.
Merz's CDU fell to 18.5% from 37.1% in ​2021, a ​setback ⁠in a state the conservatives ​have governed since 2002.
Most ​parties ⁠have ruled out joining an AfD-led coalition, ⁠meaning ​the party ​would likely need a majority of ​seats to take power.
